Miss Universe - Zozi Tunzi [5627]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Miss Universe Zozi Tunzi

We are going home with Zozi. Back to Tsolo in the Eastern Cape to meet her mum, dad, sisters and her community.
This will be the first time she is home since winning the Miss Universe title. It’s going to be epic.

Here is her bio link on Wiki.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zozibini_Tunzi

This is her programme at Tsolo

8 Feb Arrival at Mthatha airport and small press conference.
Float Parade from airport to home village in Tsolo from 5 pm.

9 Feb Wall painting unveiling at Library and lunch reception at Home.

Notes

Three women from South Africa have won the title of Miss Universe - Margaret Gardiner in 1978, Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters in 2017 and Zozibini Tunzi in 2019.

Zozi entered Miss Soundowns 2016, Miss SA in 2017 but only made top 26, Miss SA 2019 and Miss Universe 2019.

Prior to winning Miss South Africa, Tunzi was completing a Bachelor of Technology graduate degree in public relations management at Cape Peninsula University of Technology, and worked as a graduate intern in the public relations department of Ogilvy Cape Town.


We can get footage of her Miss Universe win and Miss SA win.

Issues to cover

- Her story. From Tsolo to New York
- Her parents.

- Hair. In 2017 she made top 26 in Miss SA. She was wearing long hair. "I've dreamt about it so many times but the reality of it all is much greater. So many great Queens have come before me and I hope I continue the streak of amazing women who have contributed so much to society. So here sits the crown, beautifully so on my kinky coarse hair. I hope I make South Africa proud."

- If at first you don’t succeed. Trying for Miss SA second time in 2019.
- Her values.Teaching girls leadership. She said: “I think the most important thing we should be teaching young girls today is leadership. It’s something that has been lacking in young girls and women for a very long time not because we don’t want to but because of what society has labelled women to be. I think we are the most powerful beings in the world and that we should be given every opportunity and that is what we should be teaching these young girls; to take up space. Nothing is as important as taking up space in society and cementing yourself.”

- Her causes. Operation Smile and Gender Violence
- Her views on Beauty Pageants in 21st Century
- Celebrity status – Trevor Noah and Oprah
- American Beauty Titles all won this year by black women.
Prizes. Does she have to give back Miss SA money? According to Esquire Magazine, this is what Zozi walks away with:
• A year-long salary as Miss Universe
• Luxury accommodations in a New York City apartment for the duration of her reign, including living expenses
• A modelling portfolio by leading fashion photographers
• Dermatology and skincare services
• A professional health and nutrition consultation
• Dental services
• Professional representation by The Miss Universe Organization
• Extensive travel representing sponsors and charitable partners
• Access to various events including casting opportunities, movie premieres, screenings, Broadway shows, and launch parties
• Personal appearance wardrobe and styling by the official Miss Universe Organization fashion stylist.

- After Miss Universe then what?
- Feelings about support from SA and what this means for our country.

Press Release:


Miss Universe: Zozibini Tunzi
From Tsolo to the world – since being crowned Miss Universe, South Africa’s Zozibini Tunzi isn’t just another ordinary pageant winner. With her electrifying words, demanding that women “take up space” wherever they go, Tunzi is challenging stereotypes and leading the way in the empowerment of women worldwide. Carte Blanche celebrates a woman who’s captivating the world.
Producer: Carol Albertyn Christie | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


Miss Universe – Zozi Script



How many good Miss South Africa

V/O
Chanting her name, the air rippled with excitement as thousands of people pressed against the security barriers at Mthatha airport hoping to get a glimpse of their new Miss Universe.
Zozibini Tunzi was coming home for the first time, after beating the world’s most beautiful women in Atlanta at the end of last year.

Up Sound
Now we’re down to South Africa and Puerto Rico.

Lungisa
“I felt uncomfortable on the seat.”

Zozi’s mother and father’s nerves were on edge at the finals.

“It felt as though my knees were weak.”

Up Sound

“ The new Miss Universe is…. South Africa.”

Zozi

“I probably stood there and nodded my head for a few seconds because its something…It’s unbelievable, it’s a feeling I can never describe to people when they ask. Because you have 90 beautiful women they are all smart and intelligent. It’s shock but at the same time you have worked so hard to be in that moment.. It felt like gratitude.”

V/O
Gratitude for the incredible journey that has taken her from her quiet village in the Eastern Cape to international stardom.

“I grew up in Tsolo in a village, you know the eastern cape is where dreams really die, you know we are not even allowed to dream , if I can say it because of circumstances where people come from, we come from difficult circumstances.”

V/O
She says you can’t be what you can’t see and hopes that her achievements will inspire young women.




Zozi
“It’s never just been my story and I answered in the Miss Universe stage, I said the reason why I feel that I should be the next Miss Universe is because young girls who look like me, young girls who have felt, like me even if their skin is not brown like mine, at some point in their lives they have felt that they don’t belong. I should win because I wanted them to look at my face and see their faces reflected in mine. “

V/O
The calibre of pageantry has changed considerably over time, women now are far more conscious of being agents of change. When Zozi spoke at the Miss Universe finals the world took note.

Zozi’s Mum Philiswa Nadopu-Tunzi is the head mistress of a local school.

Philiswa
“When she was on the top 5, aw wee I know her, just give her something to say then you will hear her.”

Zozi
“I think the most important thing we should be teaching girls today is leadership, it is something that is lacking in young girls and women for a very long time, not because we don’t want to but because of what society has labelled us to be.”

“I think we are the nost powerful beings in the world. That is what we should be teaching these young girls is to take up space, nothing is as important as taking up space in society and cementing yourself.”

Lungisa
She is a firm believer to herself , once I am given a space, I will use it and occupy it, I will make it a point that it works for me.

V/O
Her message struck a chord with powerful people. Oprah agreed with her and said leadership is what we should be teaching young girls.

V/O
Zozi’s father is also an educator and has encouraged her to break out from a world of patriarchy, inspiring her with his wisdom and videos on twitter.

Up Sound
“Are you different from boys what is the philosphy here?”

“We are the same, equal , we share duties it is not boys who do ama cows they must do the chores. And we want to know that washing the dishes is not a joke.”




Lungi
“I sent it to her so that and she loved it and saw it on twitter and it was trending , because it was speaking to something that is very close to her heart.”

V/O
Zozi is championing the cause of girls taking up space no matter where they come from. Her road to success started with a degree in public relations in Cape Town. Through modelling she believed she could carve a way in the world. At that time, she was sporting a very different look.

Masa
“A lot has been said about your hair, now you entered miss SA in 2017 and were sporting a long weave made it to the top 26 and then you come back in 2019 rocking a fabulous natural hair and you win.”

Zozi
“And I remember I was nervous to cut my hair because I thought I would not be beautiful anymore. And I remember looking in the mirror for the first time and thinking I don’t think I have ever seen myself this way, I don’t think I have ever looked more beautiful or felt more beautiful. “

V/O
There was subtle pressure to go with a weave again when she re entered Miss South Africa in 2019.

Zozi
“If you are asking me to go with a weave it means that you don’t think my african hair is worthy of being on a beauty platform and I think that pushed me even more to stick to my decision.”

V/O
Zozi, far more assured of who she is, walked away with the title Miss South Africa.

Up Sound
“Zozibini Tunzi”

Masa
“The Zozi Tunzi hairstyle has become very famous and I see the mother also sporting the hairstyle?”

Philiswa
“She just wanted to find herself as Zozibini, not faking anything. I just can’t say maybe she copied from me. Because I have been like this for so many years but now people see Zozibini as famous somebody they think I copied her. But it was me first.”


V/O
South Africa as a nation, is known for its beauty queens, in the past 6 years we have won 3 international titles.

Masa
“Some people have questioned the relevance of beauty pageants in todays society, whats your response to people who have questions about it?”

Zozi
“When I did beauty pageants for the first time, my main reasoning was I didn’t wake up and think I am the most beautiful girl in South Africa so I’m going to do this. I woke up and thought I have a voice, things that I want to say, I need a leadership position, I need a visible position where people can hear the things I want to say, Just sometimes need this platform to be able to stand there and speak about the things that we are passionate about. And to stand up for people who are not able to stand up for them selves.’

Miss SA

Through all the darkeness that South African women face emotional physical sexual economic abuse, what reason do we have to keep smiling?”

Zozibini
We have absolutely no reason to keep smiling because South African women are dying every day and mostly people are doing nothing about it.
I think it’s time we stop asking women what to do and start asking perpetrators to do better. To be better. To start treating women the way they deserve to be treated it is not up to us and it is up to the perpetrators to start doing right.”

Link
It’s kind of hard to imagine the little girl who used to run around these hills is now living her best life in New York City.

V/O
The worlds that have opened for Zozi have literally take her breath away.
She has addressed the United Nations and been on the Trevor Noah show and she now has millions of social media followers. With her incandescent energy she is comitted to creating change in her reign as Miss Universe.

Masa
“We see you get your first hot dog catch your first cab, but what does your day actually entail?”

Zozi
It’s a women empowerment job that we do there, to speak on the causes to help raise funds, obviously there is glamour to it. There’s fashion shows, there’s photoshoot and appearance. It’s a modern day superwomen and I am enjoying it so much.”






Promo 1 – Touch down

Incandescent Miss Universe, Zozibini Tunzi touches down on home soil. We celebrate her inspiring journey with her family as she brings the crown to her village of Tsolo.

Promo 2 – win two pageants

They say Zozibini Tunzi has that X factor, an infectious energy and drive.
How did the girl from Tsolo in the Eastern Cape become the queen of the universe?


Promo 3

She is beautiful and has broken the mold, the words “take up space” have now become every girl’s mantra. But how did South Africa’s Miss Universe, Zozibini Tunzi, manage to captivate our hearts?

It’s a modern day superwomen and I am enjoying it so much.” Promo 1 – Touch down Incandescent Miss Universe, Zozibini Tunzi touches down on home soil. We celebrate her inspiring journey with her family as she brings the crown to her village of Tsolo. Promo 2 – win two pageants They say Zozibini Tunzi has that X factor, an infectious energy and drive. How did the girl from Tsolo in the Eastern Cape become the queen of the universe? Promo 3 She is beautiful and has broken the mold, the words “take up space” have now become every girl’s mantra. But how did South Africa’s Miss Universe, Zozibini Tunzi, manage to captivate our hearts?

metadata.Further information: Miss Universe Zozi Tunzi We are going home with Zozi. Back to Tsolo in the Eastern Cape to meet her mum, dad, sisters and her community. This will be the first time she is home since winning the Miss Universe title. It’s going to be epic. Here is her bio link on Wiki. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zozibini_Tunzi This is her programme at Tsolo 8 Feb Arrival at Mthatha airport and small press conference. Float Parade from airport to home village in Tsolo from 5 pm. 9 Feb Wall painting unveiling at Library and lunch reception at Home. Notes Three women from South Africa have won the title of Miss Universe - Margaret Gardiner in 1978, Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters in 2017 and Zozibini Tunzi in 2019. Zozi entered Miss Soundowns 2016, Miss SA in 2017 but only made top 26, Miss SA 2019 and Miss Universe 2019. Prior to winning Miss South Africa, Tunzi was completing a Bachelor of Technology graduate degree in public relations management at Cape Peninsula University of Technology, and worked as a graduate intern in the public relations department of Ogilvy Cape Town. We can get footage of her Miss Universe win and Miss SA win. Issues to cover - Her story. From Tsolo to New York - Her parents. - Hair. In 2017 she made top 26 in Miss SA. She was wearing long hair. "I've dreamt about it so many times but the reality of it all is much greater. So many great Queens have come before me and I hope I continue the streak of amazing women who have contributed so much to society. So here sits the crown, beautifully so on my kinky coarse hair. I hope I make South Africa proud." - If at first you don’t succeed. Trying for Miss SA second time in 2019. - Her values.Teaching girls leadership. She said: “I think the most important thing we should be teaching young girls today is leadership. It’s something that has been lacking in young girls and women for a very long time not because we don’t want to but because of what society has labelled women to be. I think we are the most powerful beings in the world and that we should be given every opportunity and that is what we should be teaching these young girls; to take up space. Nothing is as important as taking up space in society and cementing yourself.” - Her causes. Operation Smile and Gender Violence - Her views on Beauty Pageants in 21st Century - Celebrity status – Trevor Noah and Oprah - American Beauty Titles all won this year by black women. Prizes. Does she have to give back Miss SA money? According to Esquire Magazine, this is what Zozi walks away with: • A year-long salary as Miss Universe • Luxury accommodations in a New York City apartment for the duration of her reign, including living expenses • A modelling portfolio by leading fashion photographers • Dermatology and skincare services • A professional health and nutrition consultation • Dental services • Professional representation by The Miss Universe Organization • Extensive travel representing sponsors and charitable partners • Access to various events including casting opportunities, movie premieres, screenings, Broadway shows, and launch parties • Personal appearance wardrobe and styling by the official Miss Universe Organization fashion stylist. - After Miss Universe then what? - Feelings about support from SA and what this means for our country.

metadata.Viewing Notes: Producer: Carol Albertyn Christie CF, WG, AMvN, BB WG notes: It's flat We don't get any insight into her --- it's thin and flat ---- the most intellectual part is the leadership comment. Did she say anything more profound... Anything from the parents... What does she mean for SA... Ipad on Masa's lap. Needs a transition to the EC... no segway ... Need to go deeper in the script – we don’t get her uniqueness and intelligence “Taking up space”… needs to be better contextualised – need to narrate Layer of questions seem flat/one-dimensional… need to narrate more in the NARRATE: What’s she going to mean for South Africa? Masa feels airdropped into the story – is there nothing more immersive with her? Spend too much time on the hair, but that falls flat Script transition into the green hills of Eastern Cape Script needs a re-think… needs more narration to bring some poetry to the story...it’s too flat Need HER PERSONAL story – not beauty pageant comments/bland cliche statements Narrate moving to NY; dealing with homesickness SA has been successful on the world stage – needs substance Lose Masa iPad SCRIPT – don’t say we interviewed her in Mandela’s house.. DO something with the location, but we don’t script like that
